rubrics.criterion: The patch makes the resolution-context values (the value being resolved, its parent object, and the evaluation context) travel as members of one named parameter object at the seams that resolve references against them — reference casting on the Reference seam, message-parameter resolution and ref unwrapping used by the validation context, and default-value derivation — instead of re-declaring and re-forwarding the three values positionally.
rubrics.rationale: This trio is the most repeated bundle in the case: it is re-declared at the reference, message-param, ctx-resolve and default seams on the Reference and validation-utility sides. Carrying it as one describable object is the core resolution of this instance's smell, independent of which object name or type shape the solver chooses.

rubrics.criterion: The patch models the nested-validation site description (the field key or entry index, the parent value, the parent path, the original pre-cast parent value, and the current options) as a single parameter object, so object fields, array/tuple entries and lazy nested schemas no longer receive that bundle as a fixed six-slot positional list.
rubrics.rationale: The nested-site descriptor is the second bundle of this case and the one whose positional order hurts most when extended; the shared implementation sites are the base schema's nested-test factory and the lazy schema's delegation.

rubrics.criterion: The patch rebuilds the queued-test protocol so the run context (the value, its path, the options, the original value and the schema, with the panic/next callbacks either included in one protocol object or kept as a minimal trailing pair) is exchanged through a named object between the protocol type, the validation implementation, the runner and its dispatch sites — the long positional invocation chains are gone.
rubrics.rationale: The test-run protocol is the third bundle: the protocol type, the validate implementation and the runner all re-declare value/path/options/originalValue/schema positionally and dispatch them positionally. Any sound repair must carry this context as one protocol object; keeping callbacks separate is an accepted sound shape as long as the data context is bundled.

rubrics.criterion: After the patch, the type-level contracts agree with the implementations they govern: the shared schema-interface member that was widened to a long positional list takes the same object shape its implementors use, and other protocol type declarations no longer re-state positional orderings that runtime signatures repeat.
rubrics.rationale: In this case the value bundles are re-typed at the contract level as well; a repair that only converts implementations while leaving a widened positional interface declared (which the test suite cannot observe at runtime) is incomplete. The criterion is agreement, not any particular type name.

rubrics.criterion: The patch carries every internal call site along: positions that were previously filled with literal placeholders (e.g. an undefined slot for a path the caller did not have), decompositions of the caller's own options object, and forwarding sites that re-listed the values are updated to construct and pass the new bundle objects, with no leftover call site still re-listing the old positional order against a repaired signature.
rubrics.rationale: The injected diff touched call sites in five files beyond the signature owners; the repair is only consistent if the call-site ripple is completed in the same design, since stale positional call sites are exactly how this kind of drift compounds.

rubrics.criterion: The recursive collection validators build their nested tests through the same site-description abstraction for both keyed fields (object schemas) and indexed entries (array and tuple schemas), rather than keeping two different ad-hoc parameter threads for the two access styles.
rubrics.rationale: Object fields and array/tuple entries hit the same nested-test seam with key vs index access; the instance's responsibility graph includes both, and a repair that unifies the signature but leaves differing threads at these call sites shifts the complexity rather than removing it.

rubrics.criterion: Cast-time handling of reference-typed fields passes the reference its resolution inputs through the same abstraction used by the other resolution seams, instead of continuing to pick the field's parent and context out of the cast options and hand them over as positional pieces.
rubrics.rationale: The object cast path is the one place a schema hands the resolve-context values directly to a Reference during casting; in the current state it digests options.parent/options.context positionally only to satisfy the widened reference signature, so it must follow the repaired shape.

rubrics.criterion: Default-value derivation threads its context through the new abstraction at both the base-schema level and the per-field computation for object schemas (each field's inner value/parent pair being derived through the bundle rather than re-computed as ad-hoc positional locals).
rubrics.rationale: Default derivation is a resolve-context consumer that the current state split into positional locals; because default thunks are part of the documented API, the repair must keep the bundle at the boundary while cleaning up how the inner context is computed.

rubrics.criterion: Internal option/config type aliases that the seam implementations no longer reference are either put back to work by the new threading or removed together with their last remaining use, so the exported type surface does not keep dead descriptions of the old shapes — and no import of the condition/resolve-options types is retained where the threading no longer needs it.
rubrics.rationale: The state left by the initial change carries unused internal config aliases plus a dropped-but-related options import; any bundle-first repair must decide what happens to those leftovers, and a deliberate reuse or removal is the material cleanup obligation of this task.

rubrics.criterion: The patch leaves bridge artifacts that keep the old positional form alive alongside the new abstraction — for example internal signatures that accept a leftover positional value in addition to the new object, forwarding shims that destructure the object only to pass it positionally again, or unused protocol slots kept merely to minimize the diff.
rubrics.rationale: This is the characteristic way an incomplete repair of a spread-out positional thread fails: the old order stays reachable through a shim, which is what allows the pattern to regrow. Presence of any such bridge means the cleanup is not finished; `yes` means the bridge artifacts are present.

rubrics.criterion: The documented public surface changed: the options objects accepted at public resolve/describe/default entry points, the cast/validate/isValid/validateAt/validateSyncAt signatures, the test-callback context facilities (createError/resolve and the fields they expose), the objects received by when()/lazy() condition or builder callbacks and default thunks, or the standard-schema results were re-shaped, narrowed, or re-parameterized positionally.
rubrics.rationale: The internal threading is bounded by heavily-used public shapes that the entire downstream ecosystem depends on; the task's compatibility boundary makes any of these observable API changes a failure regardless of suite outcome. `yes` means such a public-surface change is present.

rubrics.criterion: The patch papers over seams instead of repairing them — for instance pushing explicit type-casts or widened `as any`-style annotations through the threading to make signatures agree, or quoting/suppressing values (nullish guards, fallback clones) that hide a mis-threaded bundle rather than resolving it where the bundle is constructed.
rubrics.rationale: Because bundles intersect through many internal seams, the tempting shortcut is to loosen types or patch values until tests pass; those changes preserve the positional confusion the task asks to remove and typically move the mis-threading into the type layer. `yes` means the papering-over is present.

rubrics.criterion: The new carrying objects are typed so loosely that they stop naming their members — for example replacing the previously declared bundle types with untyped object parameters (any / anonymous structural bags) at the repaired seams, so callers can no longer see what travels inside.
rubrics.rationale: A data-clump repair is only meaningful if the bundle is a named describable thing; swapping the positional lists for untyped bags removes the ordering hazard without producing an abstraction. `yes` means the untyped-bag regression is present.
